correctness.rationale: The domain n>=2 and 0<=t<1, Lebesgue covariance normalization, simplex baseline, and the one-sided degenerate endpoint are explicit. Radial beta/Dirichlet disintegration gives full covariance and eigenvalues; determinant multiplication yields H_n. A universal binomial generating series and sixth finite-difference calculation prove B_n=(1-t)^6 P_n with every coefficient of P_n strictly positive, so the derivative has an exact negative factorization. The t^n and thin-frustum quadratic coefficients follow by explicit expansions, with their sharpness guaranteed by positive constants. The actual standalone verify.py completed 490 exact rational/integer checks including direct covariance determinants and coefficient identities for bounded n. Finite testing is corroborative; the all-n statement rests on the algebraic argument, not on sampled checks.

value.rationale: The isotropic constant is a central affine invariant and the vertex-truncated simplex is a canonical one-parameter bridge between simplex and prism-like geometry. An exact all-dimension strict order law at each positive depth is stronger than a global extremal inequality. The elementary-looking contact rates are not a textbook renormalization: proving the sign for all dimensions uses a nontrivial positive-coefficient polynomial certificate. The exact n-th contact order at the simplex and universal opposite-end quadratic order are motivated quantitative rigidity benchmarks without claiming a global stability exponent.
